notes: The whole sheet is drawn rotated ~90deg (all the value text reads bottom-to-top), so the two DC rails run VERTICALLY down the left and right edges and every branch is a horizontal run between them. Bridge rectifier (diodes 1-4) fed by the off-frame V-AC 0, then an L-C filter, a zener-referenced BJT-PNP 15 / Op-Amp 7 / BJT-NPN 8 series regulator. THERE IS NO GND SYMBOL in this drawing or in the inventory, so no net is named '0'; n1 (left rail) is the negative DC rail and n2 (right rail) the positive one. Net map: n1 = left vertical rail, x~93-100, tapped by four T-junctions at y~48 (diode 3 anode), y~118 (diode 4 anode), y~182 (inductor 10 left), y~238 (zener 5 anode) and y~327 (capacitor 12 left), then cornering right at y~490 into resistor 13. n2 = right vertical rail, x~414-418, tapped at y~48 (diode 1 cathode), y~118 (diode 2 cathode), y~200 (capacitor 11 right), y~256 (resistor 14 right) and y~506 (BJT-NPN 8 collector). n3 = upper AC node: the middle segment of the y~48 horizontal, between diode 3's cathode (x~184) and diode 1's anode (x~346), T-joined at (309,48) by the right-hand lead of the off-frame V-AC 0. n4 = lower AC node: middle segment of the y~118 horizontal between diode 4's cathode and diode 2's anode, T-joined at (207,118) by V-AC 0's left-hand lead. n5 = inductor 10 right / capacitor 11 left (nothing taps between them). n6 = the T at (271,256): zener 5 cathode + resistor 14 left + base of BJT-PNP 15 (its base lead runs straight up from the base bar at y~302). n7 = capacitor 12 right / emitter of BJT-PNP 15. n8 = collector of BJT-PNP 15: right at y~332 to x~374, then down to the op-amp's non-inverting input. n9 = zener 6 cathode: up from the zener at x~176 to the corner at (174,354), then right and down into the op-amp's inverting input. n10 = op-amp output (bottom apex) down to the base of BJT-NPN 8. n11 = the T at (185,490): resistor 13 right + zener 6 anode + inductor 9 left. n12 = inductor 9 right / emitter of BJT-NPN 8. OFF-FRAME COMPONENT: V-AC 0 has bbox centre (256.7, -38.0) - it is entirely ABOVE the 512x512 crop and is not drawn in the image at all. Exactly two wire ends run off the top edge of the frame, at x~206.5 and x~309.5; they are symmetric about x~258, i.e. they straddle the V-AC's bbox x-span (226.5-287.0), and they are the only open ends anywhere in the drawing. I therefore paired them with V-AC 0's two terminals (index 0 = left lead -> n4, index 1 = right lead -> n3). This is also the only reading that makes the circuit work: it puts the AC source across the two AC corners of the bridge and leaves no dangling terminal. V-AC 0 is NOT marked unconnected. Judgment calls: (a) the only wire crossing in the sheet is at (206.5,48), where V-AC 0's left lead is drawn with a clear semicircular hop over the upper bridge horizontal (verified at 10x), so n3 and n4 stay separate; every other meeting of wires here is a T or a corner. (b) all four rectifier diodes are drawn horizontally with the triangle pointing RIGHT and the cathode bar on the right, giving the canonical bridge: 3 and 4 conduct from n1 into the AC nodes, 1 and 2 conduct from the AC nodes into n2, so left rail = DC-, right rail = DC+. Diode/zener terminal order is left-lead then right-lead (or top-then-bottom for the vertical zener 6) as drawn. (c) zener 5 is horizontal with its cathode bar on the right; zener 6 is vertical with its cathode bar on top. (d) BJT-PNP 15 is drawn with a horizontal base bar and the base lead leaving upward; the emitter arrow (pointing back into the bar) is on the LEFT-hand descending lead, so emitter = left lead (to capacitor 12) and collector = right lead (to the op-amp +). (e) BJT-NPN 8 likewise has a horizontal base bar with the base lead leaving upward to the op-amp output; the arrow on the LEFT descending lead points away from the bar, so emitter = left lead (to inductor 9) and collector = right lead (to n2). (f) Op-Amp 7 points downward: the input edge is its horizontal top edge and the output is the bottom apex. Because the page is rotated, the '-' mark shows as a vertical bar; it sits at x~343 and the '+' at x~363, so the input lead entering the top edge at x~340 is in- (index 1) and the one at x~373 is in+ (index 0). This is the one call worth a second look: if the +/- marks were read the other way round, n8 and n9 would swap on the op-amp only.
